newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia has won the second Test match against South Africa by two wickets, but Mark Taylor's position as a batsman is under further scrutiny. Australia is the first team to win a series in South Africa since the Proteas return to Test cricket five year ago. Page 18.

Geelong Australian Football chief executive Club Greg Durham has denied that his resignation was related to his alcohol breath test by police last week. However, he stated that the publicity has harmed his chances of being appointed as the new chairman of the Australian Cricket Board. Page 18.

Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco has claimed that evidence at his trial into drug use was tampered with and not investigated correctly. Capobianco was given a four year suspension on Monday for taking the prohibited steroid Stanozolol last year. Page17.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League referee Eddie Ward has been dropped to reserve grade following the controversial Sydney City-Wests game last week. Ward did not send off Wests prop Harvey Howard for an illegal tackle, and was involved in several other contentious incidents. Page 47.

A record four Aboriginal athletes have been named in the Australian team for the world track and field championships in August, to be held in Athens. Nova Peris-Kneebone, Patrick Johnson, Cathy Freeman and Kyle Vander-Kuyp are in the initial squad of 38.
Page 47.

The Australian Rugby Union has called on Super 12 officials to include a combined team of Pacific Island nations in a Super 15 tournament. Two more teams may be included in the tournament next season. Page 47.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League will consider a new rule requiring clubs to change their colours and designs to avoid clashes with their opponents. It is hoped the move will avoid confusion over several similar jumpers, especially when they become wet or muddy. Page B14.

Soccer coach Frank Arok is likely to stay with the Gippsland Falcons club and not return to Yugoslavia next season if certain conditions with the club are met, including recruiting at least two top-class players from overseas. Arok was intending to move back to his native country at the end of 1997. Page B12.

The Golden Slipper Stakes barrier draw was held yesterday, with favourite General Nediym receiving the favourable gate four. Second favourite Encounter improved in the betting for the A$2 million race after drawing barrier seven. Page B12.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League player Gavin Wanganeen, from the Port Adelaide club, will not be charged for touching an umpire during a practise match against Richmond last week, however he will still face a striking charge which preceded the incident. Page 8.

Former Australian Football League player Ron Barassi has launched the 1997 Victorian Football League season by stating that Australian rules must plan for the future to survive. He believes that the football codes must work together for all to be successul. Page 78.

Australian cycling has drafted new selection criteria to avoid any future selection controversies. The criteria states that pursuit athletes must remain under the supervision of the national coach from the time of selection until the world titles. Page 7.

Basketball Australia has launched a Winter of World Basketball series, which includes tours by a Croatian men's side and Japanese and Russian women's teams. The world under-22 men's championships will also be held in August of this year. Page 71.

Melbourne will host the first International Greyhound Racing Carnival, commencing later this year. Greyhounds from England, Ireland and the United States will compete in various events which total over A$200,000 in prize money. Page 71.

The World Superbike Championships will be held at Phillip Island this weekend. Australian Superbike champion Peter Goddard has recovered from injuries sustained during a crash two weeks ago and will compete. Page 70.
